data.description:
## Problem

`scripts/import_rebar_tickets.py` creates a ticket for every imported Jira row, then transitions it to the status the Jira export declared. When that transition fails, the failure is discarded.

```python
target = _rebar_status(jira_status)
if target != "open":
    try:
        rebar.transition(
            ticket_id, "open", target, force=True, reason="jira import",
            repo_root=str(repo_root),
        )
        report.transitioned += 1
    except rebar.RebarError:
        pass
```

`ImportReport` carries only `created`, `skipped` plus `transitioned`. There is no record of a failure. The ticket is already appended to `report.created`, so it counts as imported. `main` prints a summary built from those three fields and ends with an unconditional `return 0`.

The result is that a Jira ticket which was `closed` or `in_progress` is created, fails to transition, and remains `open`, while the run reports success and exits 0. Nothing on the console or in the exit code tells the operator which tickets carry the wrong status.

The operator-visible consequence is that finished Jira work reappears as ready work, so `rebar ready` can hand the platform a ticket that was completed long ago.

## Scope

The live pilot store was checked and is not affected. All 6 tickets hold their intended status, 4 closed plus 2 in_progress, with none stranded at `open`. This defect is latent rather than active, and the next larger import is where it would surface.

## Approach

Record the failure rather than discarding it, then surface it in both the summary output and the exit code.

- Add a frozen `FailedTransition` dataclass holding the ticket reference, the target status, plus the error text.
- Add `failed_transitions: list[FailedTransition]` to `ImportReport`, defaulting to empty.
- Bind the exception in the `except rebar.RebarError` clause and append a `FailedTransition` instead of passing.
- Print one line per failed transition in `main`, naming the ticket, the target status, plus the error.
- Return 1 from `main` when the list is non-empty, so a caller that checks the exit code learns the import was incomplete.

`force=True` is kept. The importer reconstructs a status Jira already recorded rather than asserting new work, so bypassing the gates is correct here and is not what this ticket changes.

The ticket is still created when a transition fails. Discarding it would lose the imported content, and a ticket at the wrong status is recoverable once the operator knows which one it is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `import_xlsx` records a failed transition in `ImportReport.failed_transitions` rather than discarding it, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_import_rebar_tickets.py -k failed_transition_is_recorded`
- [ ] A failed transition leaves `ImportReport.transitioned` unincremented, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_import_rebar_tickets.py -k failed_transition_is_recorded`
- [ ] A ticket whose transition failed is still created in the store, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_import_rebar_tickets.py -k failed_transition_is_recorded`
- [ ] `main` returns a non-zero exit code when any transition failed, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_import_rebar_tickets.py -k main_exits_non_zero`
- [ ] `main` prints a line naming each ticket whose transition failed, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_import_rebar_tickets.py -k main_reports_each_failure`
- [ ] The existing importer tests still pass, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_import_rebar_tickets.py`

## Testing

Three tests are added to `tests/unit/test_import_rebar_tickets.py`, which already builds a real rebar store through the `store` fixture plus xlsx fixtures through `_write_xlsx`.

The first monkeypatches `rebar.transition` to raise `rebar.RebarError`, imports a row whose Jira status maps to something other than `open`, then asserts three things about the returned report. One failure is recorded with the target status, `transitioned` stays at 0, and the ticket is present in the store at status `open`. Against the current code this fails, because `failed_transitions` does not exist.

The second calls `main` with the same monkeypatched failure and asserts the return value is non-zero. Against the current code this fails, because `main` always returns 0.

The third captures stdout through `capsys` and asserts the printed output names the ticket that failed. Against the current code this fails, because nothing is printed about failures.

Commands:

- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_import_rebar_tickets.py`
- `.venv/bin/ruff check scripts tests`
data.title: ADEVX-137 Report Jira import transition failures instead of discarding them
